checks: Complete interval coverage for both controllers
Independent physical and economic reference audit
Identical weather and original decision assumptions within each comparison
Explicit solver termination, fallback and incomplete attempts
comparison: Reserve minus baseline, paired within each fully resolved case. Report arithmetic means, ranges and counts. Three seeds are descriptive evidence, not a population confidence claim.
limits: Illustrative hourly plant with ideal battery, CO2 and temperature observations.
No gas quality, pressure dynamics, essential protection loads or calibrated recovery/repair model.
A changed plant is a new application of the protocol; older results remain scoped to their recorded configurations.
Time-limited solver and hardware effects can change numerical reruns.
An observed reserve/output association does not identify a unique causal mechanism; event links show recorded evidence.

metric_definitions.assumed_contribution_eur: Assumed methane value minus variable inputs and wear proxies; original decision prices.
metric_definitions.forced_downtime_hours: Count of intervals flagged forced_trip; not all time without production.
metric_definitions.methane_kg: Sum of applied methane_kg over all executed intervals; no terminal credit added.
metric_definitions.terminal_battery_kwh: Battery inventory after the final executed interval; kWh, not revenue.
metric_definitions.total_eur: Allocated period cost from the recorded cost model, including fixed allocation.

policy_tuning: Frozen coefficients and equal planning budgets. No tuning on these evaluation cases and no training in this protocol.
question: Does a linear value for battery energy at the planning horizon improve sustained methane production under forecast error, and does the effect change with battery capacity?
rationale: Compare two otherwise identical methane planners. One credits ending battery energy at 0.01 kg CH4-equivalent per kWh; the other assigns no terminal value. This deliberately simple continuation assumption tests an interpretable reserve mechanism. It is not a stochastic controller or a verified shutdown/restart reserve.

resolution.battery_capacity: Multiply the basis capacity by each declared factor.
resolution.battery_power: Hold the basis absolute charge/discharge power fixed; adjust C-rate when capacity changes.
resolution.faults: No equipment or sensor faults in this study; capacity=1, flow bias=0, delivery delay=0.
resolution.feedstock_and_temperature: Use resolved basis inventories and deliveries. Reactor initially follows the first ambient value; both subsystems are off.
resolution.horizon: 24 hours, extending beyond the scoring window where saved forecast inputs permit.
resolution.initial_energy: Hold the basis initial SOC fraction fixed; record resolved starting kWh.
resolution.plant_basis: Reference fixture or the active run’s complete plant, cost, sensor and implementation configuration.
resolution.randomness: Named sensor channels with identical standardized draws by seed/channel/hour; observations can differ with the policy’s physical trajectory.
resolution.terminal: Report all ending inventories and temperature. Terminal planning credit is neither methane output nor sale proceeds.
resolution.warmup: No excluded warm-up. Startup costs and empty reference inventories count in the stated window.
resolution.weather: Versioned synthetic generation, start 2026-07-10, frozen snapshots. Same exogenous weather for a given seed/condition across controllers and battery variants.

review.scope: Protocol and interpretation rules specified before the first study execution.

reference.purpose: Fixed reference comparison over three days, six weather/seed pairs per capacity.

sensitivity.purpose: Extend the capacity range; retain the same controls and comparison.

smoke.purpose: Exercise the research workflow; too short and small for the reference finding.

title: What is tomorrow’s battery energy worth?
